implementation_notes: Kotlin has no Pact client of its own; the JVM realization is pact-jvm, whose Class-based extension discovery works unchanged from Kotlin - annotate the test class with @PactConsumerTest (or @ExtendWith(PactConsumerTestExt::class)), declare the interaction in a @Pact method returning RequestResponsePact, and let @PactTestFor(providerName = ...) start the mock server and inject MockServer into the test method. Kotlin's data classes and nullability do not change the contract, because the DSL still builds JSON: keep request bodies exact and response bodies matcher-based.
pitfalls: The @Pact method is located reflectively: a private or companion-object function is not discovered, and the failure looks like a missing mock server rather than a Kotlin visibility problem.
Gradle forks a new JVM for tests, so pact.rootDir (and pact.writer.overwrite) must be set on the test task's system properties or contracts land where the publish step does not look.
Renaming the consumer or provider string silently starts a new contract on the broker, orphaning the verified history of the old one.

variants.name: Spring Cloud Contract Kotlin contract DSL (.kts)
variants.idiom_name: contract { request { ... } response { ... } } in a Kotlin script
variants.implementation_notes: Spring Cloud Contract ships a Kotlin contract DSL: a Kotlin script using org.springframework.cloud.contract.spec.ContractDsl declares request and response with matchers (byRegex, byCommand, byNull, jsonPath), and the build plugin converts it into WireMock stubs for the consumer and a generated verification test for the provider; the spring-cloud-contract-spec-kotlin dependency must be declared explicitly. Choose it when the provider is a Spring Boot service that already runs the plugin, or when the contract must be reviewable as data rather than as test code.
pitfalls: The script is compiled by the build plugin, so a contract that does not compile fails the build before any test runs, and the script must sit in the plugin's configured contract directory.
Stubs and generated verification tests are build outputs, so a consumer testing against a stale generated stub keeps passing after the contract has changed.
Without explicit bodyMatchers the whole body is matched exactly, and any harmless provider field addition fails provider verification.
